column1: # Changes to the Hebrew speaker layer from the review pass over doubtful passages (shoresh/macula/speaker_review.py; applied last by
# build_speaker_layer.py, left out with --no-review). Each row: the word key it is keyed on, the field (speaker, first, last, drop:
# a quotation found by its first word; add: a new quotation from first to last inside parent; level: the level of the segments
# first..last; frame: the chapter's frame), the value, the reason the Hebrew gives, and its source (the reviewers and the prompt).

column4: reason
After לֵאמֹר God quotes what he (did not) say to a judge: לָמָּה לֹא־בְנִיתֶם לִי בֵּית אֲרָזִים (second plural addressees, לִי = God); a quotation one level deeper (level 4), speaker God. [split-01]
q02807.t213 cuts 17:5b-6 out of God's level-3 words at level 2; these clauses are the same first-person divine speech as 17:4b-5a and belong in q02807.2. [split-01]
17:8-14 continue God's first-person words (וָאֶהְיֶה עִמְּךָ, וָאַכְרִית) after the same messenger formula; merged into the added level-3 quotation. [split-01]

Nathan's message opened by כֹּה אָמַר יְהוָה in 17:4 runs on through 17:6 (God still speaks in first person: וָאֶהְיֶה, הִתְהַלַּכְתִּי, דִּבַּרְתִּי) until the new inquit כֹּה תֹאמַר in 17:7. [split-01]
God's words after the messenger formula continue unbroken through 17:6 (first-person qatal/wayyiqtol of God), so they stay at level 3 to the end of 17:6. [split-01]
כֹּה תֹאמַר לְעַבְדִּי לְדָוִד in 17:7 introduces Nathan's second message, which runs through 17:14 as the messenger's speech; it is not only the three words כֹּה אָמַר יְהוָה צְבָאוֹת. [split-01]

q04858.t407 (the single word הִנֵּה at level 3) is a fragment; הִנֵּה אֲנִי לֹקֵחַ … is one quotation (merged into the added one). Note: both q04858.2 and q04858.t407 start at 260370190071; this drop refers to q04858.t407. [split-02]
q04858.t409 (the single word הִנֵּה) is a fragment of the same divine quotation. Note: refers to q04858.t409, which shares its first word with q04858.3. [split-02]

God's speech (introduced by וַיְהִי דְבַר־יְהוָה אֵלַי לֵאמֹר in 37:15) begins with 37:16 וְאַתָּה בֶן־אָדָם קַח־לְךָ; the second-singular imperatives addressed to Ezekiel in 37:16 are God's, not the frame narrative. [split-02]
דַּבֵּר אֲלֵהֶם commands Ezekiel to deliver a message; the message is כֹּה אָמַר אֲדֹנָי יְהוִה plus God's words to the end of 37:19, all Ezekiel's level-2 speech. [split-02]
וְדַבֵּר אֲלֵיהֶם in 37:21 again commands a message: the formula plus God's words through 37:28 are Ezekiel's level-2 speech. [split-02]
The inquit is יֹאמְרוּ אֵלֶיךָ בְּנֵי עַמְּךָ לֵאמֹר; the speakers of הֲלוֹא־תַגִּיד לָנוּ are 'the sons of your people'. [split-02]
q03819.t320 makes 19:6-9 Jeremiah's at level 2, but the verbs are God's first person; merged into q03819.2. [split-04]

19:6-9 continue the same divine words without a new inquit: לָכֵן הִנֵּה־יָמִים בָּאִים נְאֻם־יְהוָה (the oracle formula marks God's speech, it is not a new speaker) and first-person וּבַקֹּתִי, וְהִפַּלְתִּים, וְנָתַתִּי, וְשַׂמְתִּי, וְהַאֲכַלְתִּים. So the marked segment is God's, at the same level 3 as 19:3-5 (inside Jeremiah's message q03819.1, which should likewise run to 19:9). [split-04]
וְאָמַרְתָּ אֲלֵיהֶם (19:11) commands Jeremiah to say the formula and the words that follow through 19:13; Jeremiah's message spans all of it. [split-04]
The words after כֹּה־אָמַר יְהוָה צְבָאוֹת in 19:3 are God's: first person אֲשֶׁר לֹא־צִוִּיתִי וְלֹא דִבַּרְתִּי וְלֹא עָלְתָה עַל־לִבִּי (19:5). [split-04]
אֲשֶׁר חָטָא עָלֶיהָ is a relative clause completing וְהִתְוַדָּה (third-person law text); there is no inquit and no change of speaker, so it is not a quotation. [split-05]
וְהֵבִיא אֶת־קָרְבָּנוֹ אֲשֶׁר חָטָא continues the casuistic law (third-person weqatal) with no inquit; not a quotation. [split-05]
וְהַבָּשָׂר כָּל־טָהוֹר יֹאכַל בָּשָׂר is a fronted topic of the next law clause, not speech; there is no inquit and the third-person law continues, so q00737.t47 is not a quotation. [split-06]

L00025 cuts כֹּה־תֹאמַר לָעָם off as a separate level-1 quotation by '(they)'; these words are the start of the young men's answer (after וַיְדַבְּרוּ אִתּוֹ הַיְלָדִים … לֵאמֹר) and belong in q02856. [layout-02]
The young men's speech begins at כֹּה־תֹאמַר לָעָם, right after the inquit לֵאמֹר. [layout-02]

כֹּה תֹאמַר אֲלֵהֶם tells Rehoboam (the young men's addressee) what to say; 'I' in קָטָנִּי … מִמָּתְנֵי אָבִי and וַאֲנִי אֹסִיף is Rehoboam. The quotation itself is right (level 2, 10:10b-11 end). [layout-02]
The Israelites' words end with אֲשֶׁר־צִוָּנוּ יְהוָה אֱלֹהֵינוּ; וַתַּחְגְּרוּ … וַתָּהִינוּ לַעֲלֹת הָהָרָה is Moses' narration (second-plural wayyiqtol), back at level 1. [layout-03]
The inquit is וַיִּקְצֹף וַיִּשָּׁבַע לֵאמֹר with יְהוָה as subject (1:34); 'I' in נִשְׁבַּעְתִּי and וְלוֹ־אֶתֵּן is God. [layout-03]
וַתֹּאמְרוּ אֵלַי: Moses' addressees, the Israelites, speak חָטָאנוּ לַיהוָה; a named speaker is clearer than '(the one addressed)'. [layout-03]

הוּא רָשָׁע בַּעֲוֺנוֹ יָמוּת וְדָמוֹ מִיָּדְךָ אֲבַקֵּשׁ is God's own continued speech to Ezekiel (the consequence clause; 'your hand' = Ezekiel, 'I will require' = God), parallel to הוּא בַּעֲוֺנוֹ יָמוּת in 3:19 and וְדָמוֹ מִיָּדְךָ אֲבַקֵּשׁ in 3:20, which are level 1. No inquit; not a quotation. [layout-04]
The inquit is בְּאָמְרִי לָרָשָׁע: 'when I say to the wicked', so the speaker of מוֹת תָּמוּת is God ('I'), not the one addressed. [layout-04]

God's speech to Ezekiel (בֶּן־אָדָם הִנָּבֵא … וְאָמַרְתָּ אֲלֵיהֶם) does not stop at 34:6; 34:7 לָכֵן רֹעִים שִׁמְעוּ אֶת־דְּבַר יְהוָה continues the prophecy Ezekiel is told to speak, and 34:8 resumes God's first person (חַי־אָנִי, צֹאנִי). It should run on through the chapter's oracle (at least to the passage end here). [layout-05]

Ezekiel's message to the shepherds (from לָרֹעִים כֹּה אָמַר אֲדֹנָי יְהוִה) continues with his own call לָכֵן רֹעִים שִׁמְעוּ אֶת־דְּבַר יְהוָה (YHWH in third person, so the messenger, level 2) and the next divine words; it is not narrative frame at level 0. [layout-05]
פֶּן־יַסִּית אֶתְכֶם חִזְקִיָּהוּ לֵאמֹר יְהוָה יַצִּילֵנוּ: after the inquit, Hezekiah's words (נוּ = 'us') are a quotation inside the king's words (level 3), like 36:15. [layout-06]

q03413.t274 gives 36:17-19 to Hezekiah, but 'I' there is the Assyrian king (בֹּאִי, וְלָקַחְתִּי, מִיָּדִי) and Hezekiah is spoken of in the third person (פֶּן־יַסִּית אֶתְכֶם חִזְקִיָּהוּ); merged into the king's quotation. [layout-06]
q03413.4 (36:20, no speaker) is the end of the same royal speech (מִיָּדִי); merged into the king's quotation. [layout-06]
The king's words after כִּי כֹה אָמַר הַמֶּלֶךְ אַשּׁוּר run without a new inquit through 36:20: first person of the king עַד־בֹּאִי וְלָקַחְתִּי אֶתְכֶם (36:17), מִיָּדִי (36:19, 20). [layout-06]

q03413.1 is a real quotation (after Rabshakeh's messenger formula כֹּה אָמַר הַמֶּלֶךְ) but has no speaker; the words אַל־יַשִּׁא לָכֶם חִזְקִיָּהוּ are the king's, one level under Rabshakeh. Its extent (36:14b-16a, with Hezekiah's words in 36:15 one level deeper) is right. [layout-06]
W00327 is a fragment of God's speech (30:5b-7 הוֹי); merged into q03963. Note: refers to W00327. [layout-07]

q03973 gives וְהָיָה בַיּוֹם הַהוּא נְאֻם יְהוָה צְבָאוֹת to Jeremiah at level 2; it is the oracle formula inside God's words (followed by God's first person אֶשְׁבֹּר), not a separate quotation. [layout-07]
כִּי־כֹה אָמַר יְהוָה is the messenger formula of the prophet (the frame); God's words begin after it. [layout-07]

The message does not stop before וָאֶתֵּן אֹתָם לְאַהֲרֹן (7:34b): it is the second half of the same sentence as לָקַחְתִּי (same speaker 'I', same object). 7:35 זֹאת מִשְׁחַת אַהֲרֹן is the narrator's summary. [layout-08]

דַּבֵּר אֶל־בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לֵאמֹר: the law that follows is the message Moses is told to say to the Israelites (second plural תִּתְּנוּ, שַׁלְמֵיכֶם in 7:32 addresses them), so by convention 7 it is a quotation inside God's command whose speaker is Moses. [layout-08]

The rhetorical questions of 3:3-5 (הֲיֵלְכוּ שְׁנַיִם יַחְדָּו …) have no formula and no divine first person; they lead to 3:7-8 where the prophet speaks of God in the third person (אֲדֹנָי יְהוִה דִּבֶּר מִי לֹא יִנָּבֵא). This is Amos's own voice in the frame. [oracle-01]
וְהוּא יֹאמַר אֱלֹהָי: the people ('he' = Lo-Ammi) answer 'my God'; level 2 inside God's speech. [oracle-02]

וְאָמַרְתִּי לְלֹא־עַמִּי is God's own first-person clause (I = God), continuing God's speech of 2:16-25 (וּזְרַעְתִּיהָ לִּי … וְרִחַמְתִּי); it is not frame narrative at level 0. W00095 should start at least here and join the preceding divine speech. [oracle-02]

17:7-9 has no oracle formula and no divine first person; it speaks of God in the third person (יִשְׁעֶה הָאָדָם עַל־עֹשֵׂהוּ, אֶל־קְדוֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל), so it is Isaiah's own voice in the frame, not God's quotation. [oracle-03]
הָאֹמֵר לְךָ is part of God's own sentence כִּי אֲנִי יְהוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ מַחֲזִיק יְמִינֶךָ הָאֹמֵר לְךָ (God's first person, as in 41:8-13a); it is not frame narrative at level 0. [oracle-04]

אַל־תִּירָא אֲנִי עֲזַרְתִּיךָ is what God (the subject of הָאֹמֵר) says, quoted inside God's speech; W00194's speaker (God) and extent are right, but it sits one level under God's speech of 41:8-13. [oracle-04]
W00244 is the single word הִנֵּה, the first word of God's words after לָכֵן כֹּה־אָמַר אֲדֹנָי יְהוִה (הִנֵּה עֲבָדַי יֹאכֵלוּ); it is not a separate quotation. [oracle-05]
God's words start right after the messenger formula, at הִנֵּה, so q03574 should include it. [oracle-05]

אַל־תִּבְכּוּ לְמֵת … כִּי לֹא יָשׁוּב עוֹד has no formula and no divine first person; the next verse grounds it with the prophet's own כִּי כֹה אָמַר־יְהוָה, so 22:10 reads as Jeremiah's word with God's quoted word following. [oracle-06]

הַמֹּלֵךְ תַּחַת יֹאשִׁיָּהוּ אָבִיו אֲשֶׁר יָצָא מִן־הַמָּקוֹם הַזֶּה is an apposition to שַׁלֻּם בֶּן־יֹאשִׁיָּהוּ in the messenger formula (אֶל = 'concerning'); God's words begin with לֹא־יָשׁוּב שָׁם עוֹד, where q03849 already starts. [oracle-06]

The inquit is וְאָמְרוּ: the passers-by of 22:8 (גּוֹיִם רַבִּים … וְאָמְרוּ אִישׁ אֶל־רֵעֵהוּ) answer עַל אֲשֶׁר עָזְבוּ אֶת־בְּרִית יְהוָה אֱלֹהֵיהֶם, speaking of YHWH in the third person; the speaker is not God. [oracle-06]

q04077 gives 33:5 to Jeremiah, but 'I' there is God: אֲשֶׁר־הִכֵּיתִי בְאַפִּי וּבַחֲמָתִי וַאֲשֶׁר הִסְתַּרְתִּי פָנַי; it is the continuation of God's words after כִּי כֹה אָמַר יְהוָה (33:4), with no new inquit. [oracle-07]

After the closing אָמַר יְהוָה צְבָאוֹת of 3:1, 3:2-4 speak of the coming one in the third person (יוֹם בּוֹאוֹ, כִּי־הוּא כְּאֵשׁ מְצָרֵף) and of YHWH in the third person (מַגִּישֵׁי מִנְחָה לַיהוָה 3:3, וְעָרְבָה לַיהוָה 3:4), with no formula until God's first person returns in 3:5 (וְקָרַבְתִּי … אָמַר יְהוָה צְבָאוֹת). The layer itself leaves 3:3 in the frame; 3:2 belongs with it to Malachi. [oracle-08]

God's address to the Assyrian king ends with 19:28 (וַהֲשִׁבֹתִיךָ בַּדֶּרֶךְ אֲשֶׁר־בָּאתָ בָּהּ). 19:29 וְזֶה־לְּךָ הָאוֹת turns to Hezekiah and speaks of YHWH in the third person (קִנְאַת יְהוָה צְבָאוֹת תַּעֲשֶׂה־זֹּאת, 19:31): Isaiah's own words in his message, level 1, as in the parallel Isa 37:30-32 (same Hebrew). 19:28 itself (the marked verse) is right at level 2, God, matching Isa 37:29. [parallel-03]

וְיִגְדַּל שִׁמְךָ עַד־עוֹלָם לֵאמֹר: the acclamation יְהוָה צְבָאוֹת אֱלֹהִים עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵל is said by unnamed people who magnify the name (it speaks of YHWH in the third person); the quotation lacks a speaker. Its end before וּבֵית עַבְדְּךָ דָוִד … לְפָנֶיךָ (David addressing God, 'your servant') is right. [parallel-04]

The inquit is כִּי־אַתָּה יְהוָה צְבָאוֹת … גָּלִיתָה אֶת־אֹזֶן עַבְדְּךָ לֵאמֹר: the subject 'you' is YHWH, and 'I' in בַּיִת אֶבְנֶה־לָּךְ is God. Name him rather than '(the one addressed)'. The extent (just those words; עַל־כֵּן מָצָא עַבְדְּךָ is David again) is right. [parallel-04]

Moses' command ends with the last word of 27:8 (… בַּאֵר הֵיטֵב׃); the quotation's last key 050270080091 stops one word short of the segment's end 050270080101. 27:9 opens a new inquit (וַיְדַבֵּר מֹשֶׁה וְהַכֹּהֲנִים). [parallel-05]

Ezra 1:1 has the same inquit as 2 Chr 36:22 (וַיַּעֲבֶר־קוֹל בְּכָל־מַלְכוּתוֹ וְגַם־בְּמִכְתָּב לֵאמֹר): the proclamation (herald and writing) says כֹּה אָמַר כֹּרֶשׁ מֶלֶךְ פָּרַס, so the formula is the proclaimer's level-1 speech, as the layer has it in 2 Chr 36:23. The Hebrew does not differ, so the two should agree. [parallel-06]

Cyrus's own words after the formula (כֹּל מַמְלְכוֹת הָאָרֶץ נָתַן לִי יְהוָה, I = Cyrus) are one level deeper than the formula: level 2, as in 2 Chr 36:23. Speaker Cyrus, king of Persia stays; the marked 1:3 is inside it. [parallel-06]

Lev 11:1-2: וַיְדַבֵּר יְהוָה אֶל־מֹשֶׁה וְאֶל־אַהֲרֹן … דַּבְּרוּ אֶל־בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לֵאמֹר — the plural imperative makes Moses and Aaron the ones who are to say the food law; name them rather than '(the one addressed)'. The level (2, inside God's command) is right by convention 7. [parallel-07]
Solomon quotes the first woman: זֹאת אֹמֶרֶת זֶה־בְּנִי הַחַי וּבְנֵךְ הַמֵּת ('my son … your son', the woman's 'I'); a level-2 quotation inside the king's speech. [notes-01]
וְזֹאת אֹמֶרֶת introduces the second woman's words לֹא כִי בְּנֵךְ הַמֵּת וּבְנִי הֶחָי; a second level-2 quotation in Solomon's speech, ending with the verse. [notes-01]
After וַיֹּאמֶר הַמֶּלֶךְ the king's words begin with זֹאת אֹמֶרֶת ('this one says'); that participial inquit is part of Solomon's speech, not narrative. [notes-01]

אִם־כֹּה יֹאמַר טוֹב: the subject of יֹאמַר is 'your father' (אָבִיךָ, 20:6), and כֹּה points to his words, which are just טוֹב; שָׁלוֹם לְעַבְדֶּךָ is David's own conclusion. A one-word level-2 quotation by Saul. Note: it starts inside segment 8733 (after the inquit אִם־כֹּה יֹאמַר), so the segment must be split at 090200070041. [notes-02]
וְאָמַרְתָּ: David tells Jonathan what to say to Saul (נִשְׁאֹל נִשְׁאַל מִמֶּנִּי דָוִד, I = Jonathan); naming him is clearer than '(the one addressed)'. [notes-02]

אֱלֹהֶיךָ אֲשֶׁר אַתָּה בֹּטֵחַ בּוֹ לֵאמֹר לֹא תִנָּתֵן יְרוּשָׁלִַם בְּיַד מֶלֶךְ אַשּׁוּר: after לֵאמֹר, the words attributed to Hezekiah's God are quoted directly; one level deeper (level 3). [notes-03]
The king's instruction contains the whole message to be delivered; it ends with 19:13, before the narrative וַיִּקַּח חִזְקִיָּהוּ אֶת־הַסְּפָרִים (19:14). [notes-03]
The message is one level under the king's instruction כֹּה תֹאמְרוּן … לֵאמֹר. [notes-03]

19:9 וַיִּשְׁלַח מַלְאָכִים אֶל־חִזְקִיָּהוּ לֵאמֹר: the sender, the king of Assyria, says כֹּה תֹאמְרוּן אֶל־חִזְקִיָּהוּ to his messengers (second plural); the speaker is the king, not '(he/she)'. [notes-03]

אַל־יַשִּׁאֲךָ אֱלֹהֶיךָ … is the message the messengers (subject of תֹאמְרוּן) are to say; it is not Rabshakeh (he is not in this embassy). The first person אֲבוֹתַי (19:12) is the king's, carried inside the message. [notes-03]

כִּי־יִשְׁאָלְךָ בִנְךָ מָחָר לֵאמֹר: the son's question מָה הָעֵדֹת … אֲשֶׁר צִוָּה יְהוָה אֱלֹהֵינוּ אֶתְכֶם is direct speech (his 'our God', 'you' plural) after the inquit; a level-2 quotation, speaker the son, parallel to the answer L00063.1 that follows. [notes-04]

In 6:14-20 YHWH is spoken of in the third person throughout (יְהוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ, אַף־יְהוָה, כַּאֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר יְהוָה); this is Moses addressing Israel (his speech from 5:1), not God. Only God's words to Moses in 5:28-31 (וַיֹּאמֶר יְהוָה אֵלַי) are God's, and they belong one level deeper inside Moses' speech (convention 6); 6:1 onward is Moses again. [notes-04]

6:21-7:1 is Moses' instruction to Israel (וְאָמַרְתָּ לְבִנְךָ; כִּי יְבִיאֲךָ יְהוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ — YHWH in the third person), not God's speech; God's words quoted later (e.g. 9:12 וַיֹּאמֶר יְהוָה אֵלַי) should be nested inside it. [notes-04]
Moses' speech to Aaron (וַיֹּאמֶר מֹשֶׁה אֶל־אַהֲרֹן) is אֱמֹר אֶל־כָּל־עֲדַת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל plus the message; it runs to the end of 16:9. [notes-05]

וְאַתָּה צֻוֵּיתָה (Pharaoh to Joseph, level 1) introduces a second message: זֹאת עֲשׂוּ קְחוּ־לָכֶם … וְעֵינְכֶם אַל־תָּחֹס … לָכֶם הוּא (second plural to the brothers), again for Joseph to say; level 2 through 45:20. This answers the translators' note at 45:19. [notes-06]
Pharaoh's speech to Joseph (וַיֹּאמֶר פַּרְעֹה אֶל־יוֹסֵף) runs from אֱמֹר אֶל־אַחֶיךָ to the end of 45:20, containing the messages; L00085 should be the whole speech. [notes-06]

וְגַם אָמַרְתִּי is an inquit (first-person qatal of אמר) followed by direct first-person speech לֹא־אֲגָרֵשׁ אוֹתָם מִפְּנֵיכֶם וְהָיוּ לָכֶם לְצִדִּים …, exactly like וָאֹמַר + לֹא־אָפֵר בְּרִיתִי in 2:1; a level-2 quotation by the same speaker, ending with 2:3. [notes-07]
q01353.t119 (no speaker) is the continuation of q01353.i72; merged into it. [notes-07]

The words quoted after וָאֹמַר continue into 2:2: וְאַתֶּם לֹא־תִכְרְתוּ בְרִית … מִזְבְּחוֹתֵיהֶם תִּתֹּצוּן is the second half of the same former command; the angel's present reproach resumes with וְלֹא־שְׁמַעְתֶּם בְּקֹלִי. [notes-07]
וָאֶתֵּן אֹתָם לְאַהֲרֹן (7:34b) completes the sentence begun with לָקַחְתִּי in the message; the message ends with 7:34. See also layout-08. [notes-08]
דַּבֵּר אֶל־בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לֵאמֹר (7:23): the law כָּל־חֵלֶב … לֹא תֹאכֵלוּ is what Moses is to say to the Israelites; name him rather than '(the one addressed)'. [notes-08]
Same structure in 7:29 (דַּבֵּר אֶל־בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לֵאמֹר); the message's speaker is Moses (it has none now). See also layout-08. [notes-08]

בָּרוּךְ יְהוָה אֱלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מִן־הָעוֹלָם וְעַד הָעֹלָם is the psalm's closing doxology (no inquit before it), still the song of 16:8-36a; the people's words come only after וַיֹּאמְרוּ כָל־הָעָם (אָמֵן וְהַלֵּל לַיהוָה, 16:36b). [unnamed-01]
The song given through Asaph ends with the doxology of 16:36a, before וַיֹּאמְרוּ כָל־הָעָם. [unnamed-01]
q01877.1 (no speaker) wraps David's own words וַיֹּאמֶר אֵלַי; that inquit is David narrating inside his speech (level 1, 'to me' = David), not a separate quotation. [unnamed-02]

וַיֹּאמֶר לוֹ דָּוִד … וְאָמַרְתָּ לְאַבְשָׁלוֹם: David tells Hushai (addressed in 15:32-33) what to say; 'I' in עַבְדְּךָ אֲנִי … וַאֲנִי עַבְדֶּךָ is Hushai. The extent is right: וְהֵפַרְתָּה לִי (I = David) resumes David's speech. [unnamed-03]

וְלֹא־מֵעֵבֶר לַיָּם הִוא לֵאמֹר מִי יַעֲבָר־לָנוּ … וְנַעֲשֶׂנָּה: the hypothetical words of Moses' addressees ('us', 'we' = the Israelites he addresses as 'you'), exactly parallel to 30:12, whose quotation already has speaker Israel. Extent is right. [unnamed-04]

פִתְגָמָא הֲתִיבוּנָא לְמֵמַר: 'they answered us', the subject being the elders the writers questioned (5:9 שְׁאֵלְנָא לְשָׂבַיָּא אִלֵּךְ; cf. שָׂבֵי יְהוּדָיֵא 5:5). 'We' in אֲנַחְנָא הִמּוֹ עַבְדוֹהִי and אֲבָהֳתַנָא are those elders. Extent (to 5:16 end) is right. [unnamed-05]
קָרְאוּ שָׁם introduces what the same people cry: פַּרְעֹה מֶלֶךְ־מִצְרַיִם שָׁאוֹן הֶעֱבִיר הַמּוֹעֵד (a naming/taunt about Pharaoh); a level-2 quotation. [unnamed-07]

q00737.t47 is the single word וְהַבָּשָׂר, the fronted topic of the law clause כָּל־טָהוֹר יֹאכַל בָּשָׂר ('as for the meat, anyone clean may eat meat'); no inquit and no speaker, so there is no quotation and no one to name (same as split-06). [unnamed-08]
